title: USELESS EATERS: Are alternative social models bound to fail?
description: Send us Fan Mail Is our current economic model sustainable in an AI-driven future? We kick off with an ambitious exploration of Universal Basic Income (UBI) and its profound implications. From dispelling myths about UBI to debunking its criticisms, we navigate through the transformative potential of providing an unconditional regular sum of money to all citizens. Real-world examples from the UK and Finland give us a glimpse into how UBI could operate, but is it really compatible with the real world? Could UBI inadvertently lock us into a two-tier society, with the wealthy controlling elite looking down their noses at the 'Useless Eaters'? or could it be a stepping stone towards a more equitable world inspired by Star Trek's utopian vision? This chapter challenges you to rethink the very foundations of our economic system, questioning if societal well-being and personal fulfillment could replace financial gain as the primary motivators in a post-AI revolution. We then tackle urgent global issues like climate change and resource consumption, pondering whether advancements like nuclear fusion could avert environmental disaster. A spirited rap battle adds a dynamic twist, encapsulating the spectrum of perspectives on AI's future—from utopian dreams to dystopian fears. As we contemplate new social models and the future of work in an AI-dominated era, we don't shy away from the raw frustration and rage of a generation feeling trapped by systemic inequality. Tune in for a powerful exploration of how we might build a more equitable future.
summary: Jimmy and Matt debate UBI and the social models that might follow mass automation, riffing on Brett Weinstein's 'useless eaters' warning from Diary of a CEO. They work through democratic socialism of AI, co-operative economies and data dividends, concluding most are wishful thinking while Jimmy argues for a Star Trek-style post-capitalist definition of human productivity.
keyTalkingPoints: Weinstein's argument: UBI removes purpose, incentivizes a depopulation mindset among elites, and creates a two-tier society of dependents
Jimmy's counter: capitalism's money-driven purpose system is the problem, not UBI itself — the alternative is a utopian model where productivity means creativity and community, not employment
UBI has real trials behind it — Finland ran the largest with tens of thousands of people — but no answer to who funds it when 10%+ of society is supported
The data dividend model is dead: the ship sailed decades ago, and X or Reddit locking down their data proved contribution without compensation
All frontier models being American means co-operative AI economies would end up paying OpenAI to replace their own workers — open source is the prerequisite

jimmy: UBI is not inevitably dystopian — the dystopia comes from the capitalist purpose system it is bolted onto
Long term, humanity needs a new definition of being productive that is not a job — a Gene Roddenberry Star Trek universe
If AI takes jobs wholesale in the next couple of years, massive civil and social unrest will follow fast
Frontier AI being American-owned means any alternative social model still rents its replacement workforce from US companies
matt: He agreed with Weinstein's clip despite it sending a chill down his spine — UBI risks incentivizing depopulation and removing purpose
Democratic socialism of AI, AI co-operatives and data dividends all sound sensible but are wishful thinking that has not worked even before AI
If people are not given a way to be productive and contribute, the ruling-class logic leads somewhere that ends badly for humanity
He wants the utopia Jimmy describes but cannot see people doing what it would take to get there
